name: LJ12A3-4-Z/BX inductive proximity switch
description: Inductive proximity switch in an M12 threaded metal barrel: senses iron/steel within 0-4 mm of its face without contact (common as a 3D printer/CNC endstop or bed probe). Gives on/off only. NPN open-collector output, normally open: OUT is pulled LOW while metal is detected and needs a pull-up (to 3.3 V, never to the sensor supply) otherwise; sinks up to 300 mA. Needs a separate 6-36 V DC supply. Sold as: LJ12A3-4-Z/BX inductive proximity sensor switch, NPN NO, DC 6-36 V (M12 x 58 mm nickel-plated brass barrel, 1 m 3-wire PVC lead: brown V+, black OUT, blue GND).
eli5: A metal tube that notices when a piece of metal comes very close to its tip (a few millimetres), without touching it, and tells your board. It needs its own 12 V power supply.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Brown wire: supply, 6-36 V DC from a separate supply (12 V or 24 V typical). Not the board's 3V3/5V.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Black wire (load): NPN open-collector output, pulled LOW while metal is detected, otherwise open. Needs a pull-up to 3.3 V (Sparkbench adds 10 kOhm to 3V3); never pull it up to the 6-36 V supply. Sinks up to 300 mA.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Blue wire: ground. Join it to the supply negative and the microcontroller GND.

supplierQuery: LJ12A3-4-Z/BX inductive proximity sensor NPN NO 6-36V
buildNotes: Wires: brown = VCC (6-36 V DC), black = OUT, blue = GND. Check the cable label: a few batches are coloured differently.
Power the brown wire from a separate 6-36 V DC supply (12 V is typical), never from the board's 3V3/5V. Join the supply negative, the blue wire and the microcontroller GND.

OUT is an NPN open collector, active LOW: it reads 0 while metal is within about 4 mm. Pull it up to 3V3 with 4.7-10 kOhm (the driver also enables the internal pull-up). Never pull it up to the 12/24 V supply.

Extra protection recommended: many units feed the indicator LED from the supply through the output, so an unloaded OUT can float to several volts. A Schottky diode in series (cathode to the black wire, anode to the GPIO and its 3V3 pull-up) or a PC817 optocoupler keeps the sensor's supply off the GPIO.
It only senses metal; steel is seen at up to 4 mm, aluminium and copper closer. Mount it with the two M12 nuts, face 1-2 mm from the target.

example.code:
from lj12a3 import LJ12A3
import time

sensor = LJ12A3({OUT})
while True:
    print('Metal: %s' % ('YES' if sensor.detected() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
